build.abMechanism:
DECOHERENCE-FREE in-process A/B on ONE cat9 boot's deep-accept carrier event (the BV-A/B pattern applied to the FA2-fork). At each full_attention TreeAttention decode (M=9, all 9 cat9 nodes co-resident), the hook has the live forked-FA2 inputs on GPU: query[M,H,D], the block-gathered dense_key/dense_value (context prefix + M tree-suffix nodes), the M×M decode_meta.tree_attn_bias (0 for ancestors incl self+root, -inf otherwise per _prepare_tree_attn_bias), scale, softcap, and the served output.

It re-calls the forked op (the SAME `flash_attn_varlen_func(..., tree_bias=...)` the deploy uses) TWICE on a CONTIGUOUS (non-paged) single-segment KV rebuilt from the captured dense blocks (cu_seqlens_q=[0,m], cu_seqlens_k=[0,len], max_seqlen_k=len, no block_table/seqused_k, fa_version=2, window=[-1,-1]) — exactly the established FA2-on-path oracle convention:
 (a) M=9: q_rows=[0..8], suffix KV = all 9 tree nodes, bias = full 9×9 block.
 (b) M=5 SPINE-SLICE: q_rows=[0,1,2,4,6]; suffix KV restricted to the spine nodes [0,1,2,4,6] (so the deep spine row attends to exactly its spine ancestors — identical K/V to the M=9 spine sub-problem); bias = the M=9 bias restricted to spine rows/cols (tree_attn_bias[[0,1,2,4,6]][:,[0,1,2,4,6]]). Because the spine is a strict chain, the sliced 5×5 sub-bias IS the M=9 spine bias for those keys; the ONLY thing that changes is M (query-row occupancy / kBlockM=64 MMA fragment tile + Is_even_MN predication + tree_bias q/k_offset=max_seqlen_q-rows).

COMPARE deep-spine row 6 (cat9 flat row6 = node5): row alignment is out_m9[6] vs out_m5[spine_rows.index(6)=4]; report RAW max_abs (NOT atol) per full_attn layer, plus per-spine-depth RAW and a recall_m9_vs_served cross-check (M=9 arm should reproduce the served forked-FA2 deep-spine row). VERDICT: any layer RAW>0 ⇒ fork IS M-dependent ⇒ FR13_FA2_QPAD (pad query to fixed N_PAD_Q) is REAL → build it; all-layers RAW==0 ⇒ M-invariant ⇒ NOT the carrier ⇒ 22-flip is DIFFUSE ⇒ reshape (cat8/cat7) route. Dispatch is OUR fork: tree_attn.py routes FR13_FA2_TREE_BIAS=1 decode → flash_attn_varlen_func with tree_bias → varlen_fwd_tree_bias → apply_tree_bias post-QK (scripts/fr13_patch_fa2_tree_bias.py).
build.howGated: FR13_FA2_MAB default-OFF (env defaults to "0"; checked at the top of _fr13_tree_attn_op_capture AND re-checked inside _fr13_fa2_mab_recall). The hook returns immediately when neither FR13_TREE_ATTN_OP_CAPTURE nor FR13_FA2_MAB is set — verified in isolation (returns_immediately=True with no env). The hook call site is the diagnostic capture_replacement that is APPENDED AFTER the deployed forked-FA2 decode (verified it sits OUTSIDE the fork if/else), so it only observes; it never feeds back into query/output. No default-path code was edited (save is now `if save_now`, additive; the A/B is `if run_mab`). End-to-end patch simulation (pristine tree_attn.py → phase4 op-capture patch → fork _patch_tree_attn) compiles, is idempotent on re-patch, and all asserts pass (A/B helper present, default-OFF gated, json import added, hook after the fork branch). The locked cat9 default path is byte-identical with the flag off. Flag documented in FR13_FLAGS.md.
build.feasibility:
YES — fully feasible; no blocker. The forked op IS re-callable in-process at M=9 and M=5: flash_attn_varlen_func (with the patched tree_bias param) is the live module-level callable inside the vLLM container, and the existing oracles (fr13_full_attn_multilayer_table.py::_fa2_tree_path_rows, fr13_fa2_no_bias_pristine_compare.py) already re-call it the same way and work.

PAGED-KV block_table: SIDESTEPPED. The deployed call uses paged KV (k=key_cache, v=value_cache, block_table=decode_meta.block_table). The re-call instead rebuilds a CONTIGUOUS single-segment KV from the capture's block-gathered dense_key/dense_value (key_cache[block_id,:take] per block) — no block_table is passed — exactly the established FA2-oracle convention. This also makes the M=5 spine-suffix KV slice trivial (index_select the spine rows of the dense suffix). The kernel's tree-bias addressing (context_len = seqlen_k - seqlen_q, q_offset = max_seqlen_q - bias.rows = 0, k_offset = 0) works identically for the contiguous M-row query + full-seq KV.

VARLEN cu_seqlens: handled — single sequence per carrier capture (the deep-accept event is one decode request), so cu_seqlens_q=[0,m], cu_seqlens_k=[0,len]. Is_even_MN=false still holds (cu_seqlens_q!=nullptr), which is exactly the M-dependent predication path under test, so the controlled call preserves the geometry being probed.

DTYPE: the dense KV capture is fp32; the re-call casts query/K/V to bf16 (the deployed decode dtype). The fp32→bf16 cast is COMMON-MODE across both M=9 and M=5 arms, so the M=9-vs-M=5 RAW max_abs (the verdict) is unaffected; the cast only shows up in the diagnostic recall_m9_vs_served cross-check. GPU is serialized — the in-process hook adds 2 small extra fork calls per full_attn layer at the carrier event only (FR13_FA2_MAB_LIMIT=1), negligible; the replay twin runs as a quick GPU job against banked captures with no boot.

verdict.evidence:
CARRIER (p3 deep-accept, ctx=1682 seq=1692, num_accepted=4): per-layer RAW max_abs(M_full_row6 - M5spine_row6) over the 16 full_attention layers = ZERO at L3,7,11,15,19,23,27,35,39,43,47,51,55,59,63 and 3.90625e-3 at L31 ONLY (mean_abs 6.36e-7 -> single channel, one bf16 ULP). NOT a bit-identity: RAW != 0. Verified against raw log output/fr13_fa2_mab/live/logs/fr13_fa2_mab.jsonl and CARRIER_VERDICT.json (matches the RUN block exactly).

SWEEP (14 events x 16 layers = 224 records, 0 failures): 26/224 (layer,event) cells nonzero (~12%), recurs across 14 of 16 full-attn layers at some event (only L3, L15 clean across all 14). EVERY nonzero value is an EXACT power-of-2: distinct set = {2^-12, 2^-11, 2^-10, 2^-9, 2^-8, 2^-7} = 2.44e-4..7.81e-3 = 1-bf16-ULP at the channel magnitude. This is the query-tile MMA-fragment-grouping signature (Is_even_MN=false predication + kBlockM=64 tiling + tree_bias lane offsets shifting with M) the static FA2-fork read flagged as 'shaky', now materialized as a real per-event/per-layer 1-ULP flip.

RED-TEAM of the A/B (decisive, validates it):
1) SAME K/V: both arms draw from the SAME captured dense_key/dense_value (same boot, same carrier event). M5 arm drops 4 off-spine suffix KV rows (3,5,7,8); this is a math no-op for the deep-spine row because the additive -inf tree_bias masks those columns out of softmax. PROOF it is not a KV-tile-boundary artifact: by_spine_depth shows depth 0,1,2 are bit-identical (0.0) in ALL 224 records (depth0 nonzero=0, depth1 nonzero=0); nonzero appears ONLY at depth 4 (deep-spine, 26 cells) and depth 3 (6 cells). If the KV drop perturbed the n_block tiling it would hit the root row too; it never does. Divergence is monotone in spine depth = pure query-occupancy/fragment-tile effect, NOT a slicing artifact.
2) SAME SPINE INPUT: M5 query = index_select([0,1,2,4,6]) of the same q_all; M5 bias = M_full bias restricted to spine rows/cols (index_select(0,spine).index_select(1,spine)); spine rows attend only to spine ancestors under the strict mask so the spine sub-bias == the M_full spine bias for those keys. Sound.
3) FAITHFUL TO DEPLOYED EVENT: recall_m9_vs_served=0.0 on ALL 224 records -> the M_full arm reproduces the served forked-FA2 (FR13_FA2_TREE_BIAS=1) deep-spine row exactly; the A/B observes without altering. Honest metric = RAW max_abs (not atol), per protocol.

HYGIENE: hook returns at the top when both FR13_TREE_ATTN_OP_CAPTURE and FR13_FA2_MAB are unset (fr10_phase4_patch_vllm_tree_gdn.py:11281), skips during cuda-graph capture (:11284); launcher passes FR13_FA2_MAB:-0 default-OFF -> locked cat9 default path byte-identical. Teardown clean: docker empty, 105 GiB free, swap 0.

CAVEAT (noted, does not flip verdict): the 'M=9' framing is loose -- m_full is actually 10 (9 tree nodes + 1 published root row), so the control is M=10-full vs M=5-spine-slice; still a clean 'full vs spine-only occupancy' control with everything else byte-held. Magnitude is ~1 ULP and sparse, so this proves M-dependence but does NOT alone prove QPAD closes the whole 22.
verdict.nextAction: BUILD FR13_FA2_QPAD (flag-gated, default-OFF). The A/B is sound and M-DEPENDENT, so padding the query to a fixed N_PAD_Q in the forked-FA2 (so the deep-spine row's kBlockM fragment tile / Is_even_MN predication / tree_bias lane offsets are M-invariant) is a LEGITIMATE non-reward-hack fix (our kernel still computes; no copy/dense/splice/route). Gate sequence: (1) re-run THIS same in-process MAB A/B with QPAD on -> require carrier L31 RAW -> 0.0 and the 26/224 sweep cells -> 0; (2) then e2e vs E5 (FLASH_ATTN native MTP-5, output/fr10_native_mtp5_same8_*): per-token argmax-vs-clean-teacher-force flip count + accept/event >= native 3.076 + bag-TV <= 0.0593. Do NOT claim QPAD closes the full 22 until step (2) measures it -- the diffuse GDN ~1-ULP accumulation may be a co-contributor; if QPAD zeros the carrier but flips persist, THEN go to reshape (cat8/cat7) as the complementary depth-accumulation lever. Do NOT go straight to reshape now: the fork is a proven carrier, QPAD is the correct first build.
verdict.issues: No A/B flaw found that flips the verdict. The KV-slicing concern (M5 drops off-spine suffix KV rows) is fully neutralized by the depth-0/1/2 bit-identity across all 224 records -- if the KV drop perturbed the tile boundary the root row would diverge, and it never does; divergence is monotone in spine depth = pure query-occupancy. Residual caveats (do NOT block QPAD, flagged for the user): (a) m_full=10 not 9 so the test is M=10-vs-M=5, still a valid full-vs-spine occupancy control; (b) magnitude ~1 bf16-ULP, sparse (12% of cells), single-channel -- this proves the fork is M-DEPENDENT and makes QPAD a legitimate build, but it is NOT proof QPAD alone closes the full 22-flip; the diffuse GDN per-layer ~1-ULP accumulation may be a co-carrier, so QPAD must be gated on the e2e-vs-E5 re-measure, not on the carrier RAW->0 alone.
